topic: Fundamentals and Applications of Mono- and Bi-Polar Ionomer Membranes in Electrochemical Technology
title: Fundamentals and Applications of Mono- and Bi-Polar Ionomer Membranes in Electrochemical Technology
session_title: Tutorial Session on Electrochemical Methods, Systems and Applications (Invited Talks)
abstract: Electrochemical technologies increasingly rely on ionomer membranes to mediate selective ion transport while maintaining electronic isolation between electrodes. This tutorial will illustrate elements of the underlying chemistry and physics including connecting molecular design and characterization to applications of mono- and bipolar membranes in electrolysis of water and other species and for separations via electrodialysis. Recent examples from our own work will be highlighted in this pedagogical context.

topic: Measurement Model for Interpretation of Impedance Spectra
title: Measurement Model for Interpretation of Impedance Spectra
session_title: Tutorial Session on Electrochemical Methods, Systems and Applications (Invited Talks)
abstract: The measurement model, developed in our group the 1990s with the collaboration of Prof Luis Garcia-Rubio, [1] provides a means to assess the stochastic and bias error of impedance measurements. This concept was recently published in a computer program that allows both quantification of stochastic and bias errors and regression of user-defined interpretation models. [2] The program is made available under the GNU General Public License (GPL) 3.0 that makes it free for non-commercial use. Our philosophy is that interpretation of impedance spectroscopy data requires both a physical insight into the chemistry and physics that govern the system under investigation and an assessment of the error structure of the measurement. The application of the measurement model is presented for the impedance data collected on sputtered iridium oxide electrodes designed for neural stimulation [3] and dielectric spectroscopy data in the form of complex frequency-dependent relative permittivity. The measurement model concept is general and may be applied for a wide variety of transfer-function measurements. [1] P. Agarwal, M. E. Orazem, and L. H. García-Rubio, “Measurement Models for Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy: 1. Demonstration of Applicability,” Journal of The Electrochemical Society, 139 (1992), 1917-1927. [2] W. Watson and M. E. Orazem, EIS: Measurement Model Program, Version 1.8, ECSArXiv, 2023, https://doi.org/10.1149/osf.io/g2fjm. [3] H. M. Lutz, Y. Wu, C. C. Eluagu, S. F. Cogan, K. J. Otto, and M. E. Orazem, “Analysis of Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Data for Sputtered Iridium Oxide Electrodes,” Journal of Neural Engineering, 22 (2025), 036007.

topic: Solvation Thermodynamics: Practical Techniques and Pitfalls in Electrochemical Measurements
title: Solvation Thermodynamics: Practical Techniques and Pitfalls in Electrochemical Measurements
session_title: Tutorial Session on Electrochemical Methods, Systems and Applications (Invited Talks)
abstract: Solvation can significantly influence electrochemical reactions, affecting everything from the stability of battery materials to their charging and discharging behaviors, to the energy barriers governing electrocatalytic reactions. In this tutorial, we’ll discuss how solvation impacts reactions, focusing on practical ways to experimentally quantify solvation effects. We begin by linking the Gibbs free energy of ion solvation to redox potential, highlighting the challenges of converting reference electrode–based measurements into absolute values relative to the vacuum state. We then discuss strategies for separating enthalpic and entropic contributions to solvation, with particular focus on calorimetry as a tool for directly measuring enthalpy. We’ll also examine recent challenges in using temperature-dependent measurements to isolate solvation entropy. We close by highlighting how these approaches can inform a range of fundamental and applied research questions in electrochemistry and materials science. No matter your research angle—from batteries to catalysis—this session will help you translate solvation thermodynamics into actionable insights that drive discovery.
presenting_author: Graham Leverick | Tufts University, Medford, MA
authors: Graham Leverick | Tufts University, Medford, MA
